arraydesignR

arraydesignR is the arraydesign R package as a point-and-click Shiny application. It takes a GeoTIFF of water depth, a receiver layout and a range model, maps the probability that the array detects a transmission from each water cell, and simulates tagged animals to count how often they are detected.

Install 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github(c("jakebrownscombe/detfield",
                          "jakebrownscombe/arraydesign",
                          "jakebrownscombe/arraydesignR"))

# Start the app in your browser, on the Stoney Lake depth raster
if (interactive()) arraydesignR::run_app()

To install all four positionR packages at once, see the positionR landing page.

Example

The app opens on the depth raster with no receivers. Click the map to add a receiver, or press Generate to place 20 on a grid, then press Compute coverage.

The Map tab after Generate and Compute coverage at the default settings.

Articles

  • The app, tab by tab (Get started): the app on Stoney Lake at its default settings, with the R calls that give the numbers it shows.
  • The articles of arraydesign give the code behind the app in full: comparing candidate arrays, setting how the simulated animals move, and simulating an array step by step.

The suite

arraydesignR is the application of positionR, four packages that take a telemetry study from array design to positions.

The positionR packages and the step of a telemetry study each one covers.
  • positionR, the suite
  • detqc: read, check and filter detections.
  • detfield: detection fields and positions.
  • arraydesign: design and test the performance of tracking systems.
  • arraydesignR: arraydesign as a point-and-click application.
